s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic bone pain with diffuse skeletal involvement and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
Intermittent generalized pruritus
Bilateral exophthalmos and blurred vision
Mild thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
Sclerotic changes on radiographs and intramedullary sclerosis on imaging
key_facts: 36-year-old man with no prior medical history
4-year history of diffuse bone pain
Intermittent generalized pruritus
Worsening bone pain over the past 2 months
Developed blurred vision and bilateral exophthalmos
Difficulty walking
Previous workups were nondiagnostic
Treated with analgesics, vitamin D, topical steroids, and antihistamines
Normal white-cell count and differential
Normal hemoglobin
Mild thrombocytosis
Normal renal and liver function tests
Negative tumor markers and autoimmune serologies
Mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on knee radiographs
Intramedullary sclerosis on humeral radiographs
Sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii on forearm radiographs
Bilateral symmetric uptake on 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI of the lower limbs
Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues on MRI
FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT of the brain
Bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake on CT and PET/CT of the abdomen
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration on biopsy

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similarities with Erdheim-Chester disease, but CD1a and S100 negativity in biopsy reduces likelihood

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms, elevated inflammatory markers, and potential for multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes and bone pain, although biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring bone pain and multifocal involvement, but biopsy and imaging findings are not fully consistent

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs, and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI, along with the biopsy showing diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis, are characteristic of Erdheim-Chester disease. The presence of extraskeletal involvement, such as enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues, and bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show positivity for CD1a, S100, or langerin, which are typical markers for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not typically match those of sarcoidosis, which often involves granulomatous inflammation and does not typically cause the specific radiographic and histologic findings seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: The patient's age and the presence of symmetric sclerotic changes and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis are not typical of Paget's disease, which usually presents with asymmetric and more localized bone involvement.

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not match those of chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, which typically involves recurrent episodes of bone infection and does not typically cause the specific extraskeletal involvement seen in this patient.
